# Separate Engine package identity from Brain metadata

## Context

The repository split moved Agent OS implementation into `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, but the npm-facing discovery split did not follow. At Engine `dev@915c1a01e7`, `package.json` still carries the whole organism's description and all 66 keywords, while Brain `dev@cd251a90f6` carries zero keywords.

Completed `#12241` / `#12250` intentionally curated one monorepo keyword surface before the split. This ticket is their post-split custody successor: it does not re-litigate priority ordering; it makes the Engine package describe the package that now remains.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open Engine issues immediately before creation; no equivalent post-split package-identity ticket exists. A2A in-flight sweep: latest 30 messages across read states contained no competing Engine package-metadata claim.

## The Problem

The Engine package currently publishes 66 keywords:

- 31 Engine/Body terms;
- 26 unmistakably Brain/Agent-OS terms;
- 9 organism/Neural-Link bridge terms that may legitimately appear on both packages.

Its description is likewise dominated by the cross-model swarm, Active Hybrid GraphRAG and DreamService rather than explaining the multi-threaded application engine delivered by `neo.mjs`. Package consumers and discovery systems therefore still see the pre-split monorepo identity.

## The Architectural Reality

`package.json` description and keywords are Class-3 identity surfaces under ADR 0018 and the `neo-identity-update` protocol. Framing is audience-segmented: the README may lead with the whole organism, while the npm package description must make the Engine product legible. Shared bridge terms may overlap intentionally; Brain-only terms remaining solely in Engine are drift.

No dependency, script, version, release or package-topology change belongs here.

## The Fix

Edit Engine `package.json` only:

1. Rewrite `description` around the Body: multi-threaded application engine, object permanence, worker isolation, JSON-first UI and zero-build development.
2. Keep the 31 Engine/Body keywords, subject to the existing priority discipline from `#12241/#12250`.
3. Retain only defensible shared organism/Neural-Link terms.
4. Remove Brain-only Agent OS, Memory Core, Knowledge Base, DreamService, GraphRAG and swarm-governance keywords from this package.
5. Record the exact keep/move/shared classification in the PR body.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `package.json#description` | Engine product framing in README / Introduction + ADR 0018 | Describes the Engine package first while remaining compatible with the organism apex | Preserve current wording only if the PR proves it is Engine-legible without Brain implementation | PR body | Before/after cold-reader comparison |
| `package.json#keywords` | `#12241/#12250` priority discipline + post-split subject custody | Engine terms retained; shared terms justified; Brain-only terms removed | A disputed shared term remains only with explicit rationale | PR body classification | Exact set/count diff + JSON parse |

## Decision Record impact

Aligned-with ADR 0018. No ADR change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `package.json` remains valid JSON and no lockfile change is introduced.
- [ ] Description names the multi-threaded application Engine as the package's primary subject.
- [ ] Every existing keyword is classified as Engine, Brain, shared, or dropped in the PR evidence.
- [ ] Brain-only keywords are absent from the final Engine package list.
- [ ] Shared organism/Neural-Link terms retained in Engine carry explicit rationale.
- [ ] No dependency, script, version, release, `private`, or Host/Cloud topology field changes.
- [ ] Cross-family identity review completes before merge.

## Out of Scope

README changes · Brain `package.json` · GitHub topics/description · npm publication · Engine/Brain dependency topology · generated SEO files.

## Avoided Traps

- Keeping the monorepo keyword set because it was previously curated.
- Deleting every shared organism/Neural-Link term and making the sibling relationship invisible.
- Expanding this metadata correction into package architecture or release work.
